Headline: "COP31 climate talks break down as EU and others reject resolution that omits fossile fuels"
- UN climate talks fell into disarray on Sunday when the EU and others rejected a final draft from the COP31 presidents, Turkey and Australia, as too weak.
- COP31 President Murat Kurum told the closing plenary no deal was approved: "We recognize that there is no consensus on this document."
- First UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without an agreement adopted by all.
- Ireland's environment minister Darragh O'Brien said the EU could not support the deal, largely because it does not mention fossil fuels.
- Alden Meyer (E3G): fossil fuels unmentioned in COP final decisions for more than 25 years, though "transition away from fossil fuels" agreed in Dubai 2023.
- The words fossil, oil, coal and phase out do not appear anywhere in the draft's 10-page text.
- Panama could not support the text.
- Draft acknowledged 1.5C overshoot and called for faster development of carbon-removal technologies; observers said Saudi Arabia and other large oil producers pushed to keep fossil-fuel mentions out and carbon removal in.
- Failure to agree a political declaration does not erase obligations from earlier summits or the legal and technical frameworks.
